about.title: How to read this site
about.whatText: This site brings together rainfall, water level, rain radar and road flooding data from official Thai agencies to help you decide before travelling. It takes no user reports and uses no social media content.
about.colorsText: Every status has a colour, a shape and a text label, so it can be read even when colours are hard to tell apart.
about.normalText: The value is within the normal range set by the agency that owns the data.
about.watchText: The value is above normal. Keep a close watch.
about.dangerText: The value has reached a level the agency treats as dangerous, such as a river overflowing or more than 10 cm of water on a road.
about.staleText: The data is older than its threshold, or the source sent no value, so no alert colour is shown.
about.staleBody: When data is older than its threshold (road flood sensors 60 minutes, rain and water level stations 3 hours, radar 30 minutes, forecast 3 hours, announcements 24 hours) the site shows it in grey with “Data not current” instead of its last colour, because the real situation may have changed.
about.noDataBody: Areas without sensors show “No data”. This site never confirms that an area is free of flooding. Road flood sensors exist in Bangkok only.
about.forecastBody: Bars are rain per hour (mm/h) from the Thai Meteorological Department. The line is the chance of rain (%) from Open-Meteo, because the TMD does not publish an hourly chance of rain. Forecasts are estimates, not a fixed time when rain will stop.
about.sourcesBody: Every value shown has its source name, a link to the original page and its observation time.
about.limit1: Radar updates every 10 minutes. Road flood sensors and highway reports update when someone opens the site (at most once per 10 minutes), so data may lag behind the real situation.
about.limit2: CCTV images have to be viewed on the original website.
about.limit3: Highway reports come from a Department of Highways system that may change format without notice.
about.limit4: If a source fails, the site shows the last data in grey and never estimates values itself.
about.installBody: Open the browser menu and choose “Add to Home Screen” to open the site like an app and see the last saved data even with a poor signal.
about.mapCredit: Base map: OpenFreeMap, OpenMapTiles and OpenStreetMap contributors
about.staleWhy: Rain and water level stations use 3 hours because several agencies report hourly and publish 1.5 to 2.5 hours after the observation.
about.limit5: Rainfall and water level are fetched from ThaiWater directly by your browser, because ThaiWater does not accept requests from this site's server. ThaiWater therefore sees a connection from your device, as it would when you open thaiwater.net, and each reload (every 10 minutes) uses about 1 MB of data.
about.searchCredit: Subdistrict and district positions: Thai Meteorological Department · Place names: OpenStreetMap via Photon
about.limit6: Place-name searches are sent through this site's server to the Photon service (OpenStreetMap data), so some places may be missing or spelled differently.
about.limit7: LINE rain alerts use LINE's free plan (300 messages a month, counted per recipient), so they are limited to 2 a day and 48 a month, and rely on forecasts only: rain may come without an alert, or an alert without rain.

alerts.title: LINE rain alerts
alerts.intro: At 08:00 and 18:00 a 12-hour rain outlook for every area is sent, only on days when some area expects rain. In between, an urgent alert goes out when rain or a storm within 2 hours appears that the last summary did not mention. Messages go to everyone who has added the family's LINE account.
